answer: In a proportional-odds ordinal logit model of COVID-19 severity (AESEV 1-4, AEPT=='COVID-19', n=148; BCG=TRTGRP, prior-medical-history=any MHONGO=='Yes', controlling for patient interaction frequency patients_seen), the BCG x prior-medical-history interaction is NOT robustly significant. HEADLINE (4-level, patients_seen ordinal-numeric): interaction OR = 2.89, 95% CI [2.37, 3.53], p~2e-25. However this is a quasi-separation artifact, not an identifiable interaction: the same large coefficient (coef~1.06, SE~0.10) relocates to BCG:pmh (headline), to patients_seen (3-level), and to prior-medical-history (patients_seen-categorical) across specifications, and the p-value (~1e-25 at n=148) is implausibly small. Mechanism: only 14 subjects reach severity 3-4, and 13/14 have prior medical history, so the sparse top cells let the model attribute the single strong 'severe-group' contrast to any of the overlapping predictors. Both pre-committed robustness checks flip the interaction to null: 3-level severity collapse (3&4->severe) OR = 0.94, 95% CI [0.34, 2.58], p=0.91; patients_seen as categorical OR = 0.92, 95% CI [0.46, 1.85], p=0.82. Robust conclusion: no significant BCG x prior-medical-history interaction on COVID-19 severity (OR ~0.9, CI spanning 1); the headline 4-level OR of ~2.89 should not be interpreted as a real effect.
